subject: SCI
title: Science 4
description: Fourth-grade science built on the California Next Generation Science Standards and the 2016 CA Science Framework. Students investigate energy (speed, collisions, circuits, sound, light and heat), waves and information transfer, how plant and animal structures support survival and sensing, how weathering, erosion and rock layers record Earth's history, how maps reveal patterns of earthquakes and volcanoes, and how humans use natural resources and reduce hazard impacts. Each week includes a hands-on investigation with household materials and a science notebook entry.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 California Science Framework

standards.4-PS3-1: Use evidence to construct an explanation relating the speed of an object to the energy of that object.
standards.4-PS3-2: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat and electric currents.
standards.4-PS3-3: Ask questions and predict outcomes about the changes in energy that occur when objects collide.
standards.4-PS3-4: Apply scientific ideas to design, test and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.
standards.4-PS4-1: Develop a model of waves to describe patterns in terms of amplitude and wavelength and that waves can cause objects to move.
standards.4-PS4-2: Develop a model to describe that light reflecting from objects and entering the eye allows objects to be seen.
standards.4-PS4-3: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.
standards.4-LS1-1: Construct an argument that plants and animals have internal and external structures that support survival, growth, behavior and reproduction.
standards.4-LS1-2: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process it in the brain and respond.
standards.4-ESS1-1: Identify evidence from patterns in rock formations and fossils in rock layers to support an explanation for changes in a landscape over time.
standards.4-ESS2-1: Make observations and/or measurements to provide evidence of the effects of weathering or the rate of erosion by water, ice, wind or vegetation.
standards.4-ESS2-2: Analyze and interpret data from maps to describe patterns of Earth's features.
standards.4-ESS3-1: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment.
standards.4-ESS3-2: Generate and compare multiple solutions to reduce the impacts of natural Earth processes on humans.
standards.3-5-ETS1-1: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or want, including criteria for success and constraints on materials, time or cost.
standards.3-5-ETS1-2: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each meets the criteria and constraints.
standards.3-5-ETS1-3: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

units.title: Energy and Motion
units.big_idea: Faster objects have more energy, and collisions transfer energy between objects.

units.title: Energy Transfer: Sound, Heat and Electricity
units.big_idea: Energy moves from place to place through sound, light, heat and electric currents.

units.title: Waves and Information
units.big_idea: Waves have patterns of amplitude and wavelength, and patterns can carry information.

units.title: Light and Sight
units.big_idea: We see objects when light reflects off them and enters our eyes.

units.title: Structures and Senses of Living Things
units.big_idea: Internal and external structures help organisms survive, and senses send information to the brain.

units.title: Earth's Changing Surface
units.big_idea: Weathering and erosion slowly reshape land, and rock layers and fossils record the changes.

units.title: Mapping Earth's Features and Natural Hazards
units.big_idea: Maps reveal patterns of mountains, volcanoes and earthquakes, and engineers design ways to reduce hazards.

units.title: Energy Resources and the Environment
units.big_idea: Energy and fuels come from natural resources, renewable and nonrenewable, and their use affects the environment.

units.title: Engineering Design Capstone
units.big_idea: Engineers define problems, test prototypes fairly and improve designs that convert energy.

objectives: Identify forms of energy around us

days.title: Energy hunt
days.work: Walk through the house listing 15 examples of energy (moving, sound, light, heat, electrical) in a notebook table.

days.title: Notebook setup
days.work: Set up a science notebook with table of contents and an investigation template (question, prediction, data, conclusion).

days.title: Stored and moving energy
days.work: Stretch a rubber band, wind a toy, lift a ball; describe where energy is stored and when it becomes motion.

days.title: Mystery question
days.work: Watch a Mystery Science energy intro and discuss 'What makes things go?'

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw and label a diagram of 4 energy examples and explain each in a sentence.

objectives: Measure speed using distance and time

days.title: Ramp setup
days.work: Build a ramp with a book stack and practice timing a marble over 1 meter.

days.title: Height and speed
days.work: Release a marble from 3 ramp heights, timing 3 trials each and recording data.

days.title: Cup push test
days.work: Measure how far the marble pushes a paper cup at each height as evidence of energy.

days.title: Graph and explain
days.work: Graph height vs. cup distance and write a claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz: predict and explain which marble has more energy in 4 scenarios.

weeks.assessment: CER explanation relating speed and energy.

days.title: Marble collisions
days.work: Roll one marble into a stationary marble in a ruler groove and observe what happens to motion.

days.title: Question generation
days.work: Write 5 testable questions about collisions (mass, speed, number of marbles).

days.title: Test a question
days.work: Investigate one question with 3 trials and record results.

days.title: Sound and heat
days.work: Clap hands and bang blocks to observe that collisions also make sound and heat.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing where the energy went in a car crash test video.

weeks.topic: Energy in motion: Newton's cradle and roller coasters
objectives: Model energy transfer in a system

days.title: Newton's cradle
days.work: Build a hanging-washer pendulum chain from string and observe energy transfer.

days.title: Roller coaster design
days.work: Build a foam pipe insulation marble coaster and measure speed at the bottom.

days.title: Loops and hills
days.work: Test whether the marble makes it over hills of different heights and explain using energy.

days.title: PhET simulation
days.work: Use Energy Skate Park Basics to observe speed and height relationships.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 1 test on speed, energy and collisions.

days.title: Vibrations
days.work: Stretch plastic wrap over a bowl, sprinkle rice and make sounds nearby to see the rice move.

days.title: Rubber band guitar
days.work: Build a shoebox rubber band guitar and test how tightness changes pitch.

days.title: Sound travels
days.work: Test how sound travels through air, water and a table by tapping and listening.

days.title: String telephone
days.work: Build a cup telephone and test string length and tightness.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write how sound energy moved from source to ear in each investigation.

days.title: Hot water spoons
days.work: Place metal, plastic and wooden spoons in hot water and feel which handle warms first.

days.title: Ice cube race
days.work: Wrap ice cubes in foil, cloth and paper and time melting.

days.title: Thermometer data
days.work: Measure temperature of warm water every 2 minutes as it cools and graph.

days.title: Insulator design
days.work: Design a cup cozy to keep water warm and test it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on conductors, insulators and heat transfer.

objectives: Show electricity transfers energy to light, sound and motion

days.title: Light a bulb
days.work: Use a battery, one wire and a bulb to find 4 ways to light the bulb and draw them.

days.title: Conductor test
days.work: Build a circuit tester and test 12 household objects as conductors or insulators.

days.title: Switches
days.work: Make a paper clip switch and add it to a circuit.

days.title: PhET circuits
days.work: Build series and parallel circuits in the Circuit Construction Kit.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a circuit diagram and explain how energy travels.

objectives: Design a device that converts energy

days.title: Conversion hunt
days.work: List devices at home that convert energy (toaster, fan) and identify input and output.

days.title: Define problem
days.work: Define a problem: a light-up alarm for a door; list criteria and constraints.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the door alarm with a foil switch and buzzer or LED.

days.title: Test and improve
days.work: Test the alarm 5 times by opening the door, record each result and fix one failure point (loose foil, weak contact).

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 2 test on energy transfer.

weeks.assessment: Door alarm prototype and Unit 2 test.

days.title: Rope waves
days.work: Shake a jump rope to make waves and change amplitude and wavelength.

days.title: Water waves
days.work: Make waves in a tub of water and observe how a floating cork moves up and down, not along.

days.title: Wave drawings
days.work: Draw and label waves with different amplitude and wavelength.

days.title: PhET Wave on a String
days.work: Use the simulation to change amplitude and frequency and record patterns.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz labeling crest, trough, amplitude and wavelength on drawn waves.

objectives: Relate ocean waves to coastal changes

days.title: Wave pushes
days.work: Show that larger amplitude waves move a toy boat more and measure distance.

days.title: Beach model
days.work: Build a sand beach in a tub and make waves to observe sand movement.

days.title: Ocean waves
days.work: Watch a video on California surf and tsunamis and record how waves carry energy.

days.title: Sound as waves
days.work: Connect sound waves to wave patterns with a slinky.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER on how waves cause objects to move.

days.title: Morse code
days.work: Send messages with a flashlight using Morse code.

days.title: Binary pictures
days.work: Encode a pixel picture in 1s and 0s and have a partner decode it.

days.title: Drum signals
days.work: Invent a drum-beat code for 10 words and send 3 messages to a family member in another room.

days.title: Compare codes
days.work: Compare which code is fastest and most accurate and why.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph about how patterns transfer information.

objectives: Generate and compare solutions to send information

days.title: Define challenge
days.work: Challenge: send a 5-word message across the yard without speaking.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Brainstorm 3 solutions and list pros and cons.

days.title: Test
days.work: Test each solution and record speed and accuracy.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Improve the most accurate solution to send the message faster, then retest it twice.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on waves and information.

objectives: Show light travels in straight lines

days.title: Straight lines
days.work: Line up index cards with holes and shine a flashlight through to show light travels straight.

days.title: Mirror reflection
days.work: Use mirrors to bounce a flashlight beam to a target.

days.title: Periscope
days.work: Build a periscope from a milk carton and two mirrors.

days.title: Absorb vs reflect
days.work: Compare how light reflects from foil, white paper and black paper.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw light ray diagrams with arrows for the index card, mirror and periscope setups.

objectives: Explain why we cannot see in total darkness

days.title: Dark box
days.work: Look into a dark shoebox with an object, then open a small light hole and observe.

days.title: Eye model
days.work: Draw and label the eye and how light enters the pupil.

days.title: Pupil changes
days.work: Observe pupil size in dim and bright light with a mirror.

days.title: Seeing model
days.work: Draw a model of light from a lamp reflecting off a book into the eye.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing how light allows us to see.

days.title: Rainbow
days.work: Make a rainbow with a glass of water and sunlight.

days.title: Color heat
days.work: Place thermometers under black and white paper in the sun and record temperature.

days.title: Solar energy
days.work: Build a simple solar oven from a pizza box and foil.

days.title: Test oven
days.work: Melt chocolate or s'mores in the solar oven and record temperature.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 4 test on light and sight.

weeks.assessment: Solar oven data and Unit 4 test.

objectives: Identify internal and external plant structures

days.title: Celery transport
days.work: Put celery in colored water and observe xylem transport after 24 hours.

days.title: Flower dissection
days.work: Dissect a flower and label petals, stamens and pistil.

days.title: Root systems
days.work: Compare roots of grass and a carrot and explain their functions.

days.title: California plants
days.work: Research structures of a cactus and a redwood for their environments.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an argument for how one plant structure supports survival.

days.title: Bird beak lab
days.work: Use tweezers, spoons and clothespins as beaks to pick up seeds, rice and gummy worms.

days.title: Camouflage
days.work: Hide colored paper 'insects' outside and count which are found first.

days.title: Shell protection
days.work: Test how a shell structure (egg carton) protects an egg in a drop.

days.title: California animals
days.work: Research external structures of the desert tortoise and sea otter.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning paragraph about how one external structure (e.g., a sea otter's dense fur) helps it survive.

days.title: Skeleton
days.work: Examine cleaned chicken bones and compare to human bones.

days.title: Lung model
days.work: Build a lung model from a plastic bottle, two balloons and a straw and pull the diaphragm balloon to model breathing.

days.title: Heart
days.work: Measure pulse at rest and after exercise and explain the heart's job.

days.title: Digestion
days.work: Model digestion with a plastic bag, crackers and water.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label a diagram of internal structures and functions.

objectives: Model how senses send information to the brain

days.title: Ruler drop
days.work: Measure reaction time with a ruler drop test 5 times.

days.title: Smell and taste
days.work: Taste apple and potato pieces blindfolded with nose plugged, then unplugged, and record how smell affects taste.

days.title: Touch test
days.work: Identify 8 fabrics and textures by touch while blindfolded and record which were hardest.

days.title: Animal senses
days.work: Research owls, bats and sharks and their special senses.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 5 test and draw a sense-brain-response model.

days.title: Shake test
days.work: Shake sugar cubes in a jar for 1, 2 and 3 minutes and observe rounding.

days.title: Chalk and vinegar
days.work: Place chalk pieces in vinegar and in water overnight and compare them to model chemical weathering.

days.title: Freeze-thaw
days.work: Freeze a water-filled straw sealed with clay and observe expansion.

days.title: Plants weather rock
days.work: Observe roots breaking sidewalks on a neighborhood walk.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz sorting 10 examples into physical and chemical weathering.

weeks.topic: Erosion by water, wind and ice

days.title: Stream table
days.work: Build a sand stream table and pour water to observe erosion and deposition.

days.title: Slope test
days.work: Test erosion at different slopes and measure sediment.

days.title: Wind
days.work: Blow through a straw at sand and measure distance moved.

days.title: Ice
days.work: Drag an ice cube with sand over clay and observe scratches like glaciers in Yosemite.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER comparing how fast water, wind and ice eroded material in this week's models, using measurements.

objectives: Use fossils to infer past environments

days.title: Layer jar
days.work: Make layers of sediment in a jar and observe settling.

days.title: Superposition
days.work: Order 6 rock layer drawings from oldest to youngest using the law of superposition and explain one.

days.title: Fossil casts
days.work: Press shells and leaves into clay to make imprint fossils and fill one with plaster or glue to make a cast.

days.title: Grand Canyon & Painted Cave
days.work: Analyze a photo of rock layers and fossils and infer past environments.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain changes in a landscape over time using layers.

objectives: Explain how Yosemite and the coast formed

days.title: Yosemite
days.work: Read about how glaciers carved Yosemite Valley.

days.title: Coastal erosion
days.work: Analyze photos of eroding cliffs at Pacifica and Big Sur and list the agents causing the erosion.

days.title: Sea caves model
days.work: Model sea arch formation with sugar cubes and water.

days.title: Sketch
days.work: Create a before/after landscape sketch with explanation.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 6 test on weathering, erosion and rock layers.

days.title: Clay mountain
days.work: Build a clay mountain and slice contour lines to make a topographic map.

days.title: Read a topo map
days.work: Read a topographic map of Half Dome and find the steepest side by looking at contour line spacing.

days.title: Ocean floor
days.work: Read an ocean floor map and identify trenches and ridges.

days.title: World patterns
days.work: Mark the Sierra Nevada, Andes, Rockies and Himalayas on a world map and note where they lie relative to coasts.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz on reading contour lines, elevation and ocean-floor features.

days.title: USGS map
days.work: Plot 20 recent magnitude 4+ earthquakes from the USGS map on a world map with red dots.

days.title: Volcanoes
days.work: Plot 15 active volcanoes (including Mount Shasta and Lassen Peak) with orange triangles on the same map.

days.title: Pattern
days.work: Describe the Ring of Fire pattern formed by the dots and triangles around the Pacific Ocean.

days.title: San Andreas
days.work: Locate the San Andreas Fault and explain why California has earthquakes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining the patterns of earthquakes, volcanoes and mountains on your map.

objectives: Compare solutions to reduce earthquake damage

days.title: Shake table
days.work: Build toothpick-and-marshmallow buildings and test on a gelatin shake table.

days.title: Improve
days.work: Add cross-bracing to the toothpick buildings and retest on the gelatin shake table, counting seconds until collapse.

days.title: Compare solutions
days.work: Build a base-isolation version on rubber bands or marbles and compare its shaking with the braced design.

days.title: Earthquake kit
days.work: Plan a family earthquake kit and practice 'Drop, Cover and Hold On' as in California's Great ShakeOut drill.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a comparison of bracing and base isolation using test data, cost and materials.

days.title: Tsunami model
days.work: Make a wave in a tub and test sea wall designs.

days.title: Landslides
days.work: Model a hillside and test plants/stakes to reduce slides.

days.title: Floods
days.work: Build a clay or sand levee along a sand river in a pan and test how well it holds back a flood of poured water.

days.title: Warning systems
days.work: Read about the NOAA tsunami warning system and tsunami evacuation signs on the California coast.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on reading maps of Earth's features and comparing solutions to natural hazards.

objectives: Identify natural resources used for energy

days.title: Resource sort
days.work: Sort 12 resources into renewable and nonrenewable.

days.title: Fossil fuels
days.work: Read about how coal, oil and natural gas formed from ancient living things and draw a 3-step diagram.

days.title: Home energy
days.work: Read a family energy bill and identify energy sources.

days.title: California energy
days.work: Read a pie chart of California's electricity sources (solar, natural gas, hydro, wind, nuclear) and list the top three.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a quiz classifying resources as renewable or nonrenewable and naming their uses.

objectives: Investigate solar, wind and water energy

days.title: Pinwheel turbine
days.work: Build a pinwheel turbine that lifts a paper clip.

days.title: Water wheel
days.work: Build a water wheel from a plastic plate and cups.

days.title: Solar
days.work: Compare the temperature of water in a black container in sun vs shade every 10 minutes for 40 minutes.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare wind, water and solar models in a chart by output, reliability and needs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an explanation of which source fits California best.

objectives: Describe environmental effects of resource use

days.title: Oil spill
days.work: Simulate an oil spill and test cleanup methods.

days.title: Mining
days.work: Model mining by extracting chocolate chips from a cookie with toothpicks and observe the damage to the 'land'.

days.title: Air pollution
days.work: Smear petroleum jelly on index cards, place them near a road and in the yard for 3 days, and compare particles collected.

days.title: Trade-offs
days.work: Discuss trade-offs of 4 energy sources (cost, pollution, reliability, land use) and rank them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about how one energy source affects the environment.

objectives: Obtain and combine information from multiple sources
Present findings on an energy source

days.title: Choose a source
days.work: Choose one energy source used in California (Diablo Canyon nuclear, Altamont Pass wind, Central Valley solar, Hoover Dam hydro, oil from Kern County) and write 3 research questions.

days.title: Research notes
days.work: Take notes from two sources on how the energy is made, where the resource comes from and its environmental effects.

days.title: Poster
days.work: Create a poster with a labeled diagram of how the resource becomes electricity and a pros/cons chart.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the poster to family in 3 minutes and answer questions about trade-offs.

days.title: Unit 8 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 8 test on natural resources, renewable vs nonrenewable energy and environmental effects.

weeks.topic: Defining a design problem: the wind-powered lifter
objectives: Define a design problem with criteria and constraints

days.title: The challenge
days.work: Read the challenge: design a device that converts wind energy from a box fan into motion that lifts 10 pennies 30 cm; restate it in your own words.

days.title: Criteria
days.work: List measurable criteria for success (lift height, load, time to lift) in a table.

days.title: Constraints
days.work: List constraints: only household materials (cups, straws, skewers, cardstock, string, tape), 3 days of building, no batteries.

days.title: Research
days.work: Study photos and diagrams of historic windmills and modern turbines and note how blades and axles convert wind to rotation.

days.title: Design brief
days.work: Write a one-page design brief with problem, criteria, constraints and a first sketch idea.

weeks.assessment: Design brief with criteria and constraints.

days.title: Brainstorm
days.work: Brainstorm at least 5 blade and axle ideas without judging, sketching each quickly.

days.title: Blade mini-test
days.work: Test 3 blade shapes (flat, angled, cupped) on a straw axle in front of the fan and count rotations in 10 seconds.

days.title: Detailed sketches
days.work: Draw three full designs with labels, materials and how energy changes from wind to motion to lifting.

days.title: Decision matrix
days.work: Score each design 1-3 on each criterion and constraint in a decision matrix.

days.title: Choose & justify
days.work: Choose one design and write a paragraph explaining why it best meets the criteria.

objectives: Plan and carry out fair tests controlling variables

days.title: Build day 1
days.work: Build the base and axle of the lifter following the chosen sketch.

days.title: Build day 2
days.work: Attach blades, string and the penny cup and do a first trial run.

days.title: Plan a fair test
days.work: Write a test plan keeping fan distance, fan speed and load the same for every trial.

days.title: Run trials
days.work: Run 5 trials, recording lift height and time in a data table.

days.title: Failure points
days.work: Identify where the device fails (blades slip, string tangles, axle wobbles) and photograph or sketch each.

weeks.assessment: Test plan, data table and failure-point analysis.

objectives: Improve a prototype based on test data

days.title: Redesign
days.work: Change one variable (blade angle, number of blades or axle material) to fix the biggest failure point.

days.title: Retest
days.work: Run 5 new trials under the same conditions and record results.

days.title: Compare results
days.work: Graph before-and-after averages and decide whether the change helped.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the device, explaining each energy conversion (wind to rotation to lifting) and the data.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on what you would change with more time and materials.

objectives: Connect big ideas across physical, life and Earth science
Demonstrate mastery on a cumulative assessment

days.title: Energy & waves review
days.work: Make concept-map flashcards for energy, collisions, circuits, waves and light, and quiz yourself.

days.title: Life science review
days.work: Redo the ruler-drop reaction test and explain the senses-brain-response model from memory.

days.title: Earth science review
days.work: Explain a photo of California coastal cliffs using weathering, erosion and rock layer vocabulary.

days.title: Cumulative test
days.work: Take the end-of-year science assessment covering all units.

days.title: Notebook showcase
days.work: Choose your three favorite investigations from the notebook and explain them to family.
